question: In April 2025, in which city of India did the Central Zoo Authority (CZA) approve the city's first deer park?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Noida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In April 2025, the Central Zoo Authority (CZA) approved the establishment of Noida's first deer park.
 
• The park is aimed at promoting wildlife conservation and providing a habitat for various deer species.
 
• The deer park will also serve as an educational and recreational facility for visitors, highlighting the importance of biodiversity conservation.
 
• Noida's initiative aligns with India’s broader goal of enhancing urban green spaces and wildlife preservation efforts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Zoo Authority (CZA):**

 
 
• The CZA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India.
 
• It was established in 1992 to oversee the management of zoos in India and ensure the welfare of captive animals.
 
• The authority plays a crucial role in approving zoo projects and monitoring their compliance with prescribed standards.
 
 
 
• **Deer Conservation in India:**
 
 
• India is home to a variety of deer species, including the spotted deer (chital), swamp deer (barasingha), and sambar deer.
 
• These species play a vital role in maintaining the ecological balance of forest ecosystems.
 
• Conservation measures are critical as some deer species face threats from habitat loss and poaching.
 
 
 
• **Urban Green Spaces:**
 
 
• Urban green spaces like parks, gardens, and wildlife reserves contribute to sustainable urban development.
 
• They improve air quality, provide recreational opportunities, and promote mental well-being.
 
• Initiatives like deer parks in urban areas encourage environmental awareness among city dwellers.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity in India:**
 
 
• India is one of the 17 megadiverse countries in the world, hosting over 7% of the world’s biodiversity.
 
• Conservation efforts in urban and rural areas are crucial to preserving this rich biodiversity.
 
• Projects like the Noida deer park highlight the importance of integrating biodiversity conservation into urban planning.
